part.name: Ergonomic housing with scroll-wheel/button in top aperture
part.description: Two-solid part: a streamlined housing (SOLID 0) with a rectangular top aperture/pocket, and a separate rounded scroll-wheel/button insert (SOLID 1) seated in/through that aperture. Exterior is predominantly freeform (B-spline) with a freeform bottom, side skins, and front/rear end-cap surfaces; aperture is defined by planar pocket walls/floor.
part.symmetry_note: Housing exterior appears approximately left-right symmetric about a longitudinal midplane; the top wheel/aperture is centered laterally. Minor asymmetry may exist due to drafted aperture walls.

Section.name: Upper housing shell (top deck)
features included: Top aperture boundary (opening edge as an inner loop on the top surface)
Blend/fillet transitions into side skins and end caps
Section.function intent: Provide the main ergonomic outer surface and structural cover; define the top opening perimeter that interfaces with the wheel/button.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a stiff, continuous shell carrying bending loads between side skins and end regions; locally interrupts the shell with an opening while maintaining stiffness via curvature and continuity into adjacent skins.
Section.geometry: Large B-spline surface spanning most of the top region with a secondary inner wire indicating the aperture boundary (cutout) in this face.
Section.location: Top of the main housing (high Y region), spanning most of the length (Z) and width (X).

major_faces.name: Top freeform deck (with aperture loop)
major_faces.description: Main top B-spline skin; contains two boundary loops indicating an opening/cutout region for the wheel/button.

Section.name: Side skins (left and right)
features included: Edge blends into top deck and bottom base
Section.function intent: Provide lateral enclosure, ergonomic side surfaces, and structural depth for stiffness; transmit loads between top and bottom skins.
Section.physical behavior: Works as two deep side webs; resists torsion and bending by increasing section modulus and providing continuous load paths along the length.
Section.geometry: Two large opposing B-spline surfaces forming the left and right sidewalls/skins.
Section.location: Outer lateral sides at X-min (left) and X-max (right) spanning most of Y and Z.

major_faces.name: Left side freeform skin
major_faces.description: Large B-spline exterior side surface on the left (X-min) of the housing.

major_faces.name: Right side freeform skin
major_faces.description: Large B-spline exterior side surface on the right (X-max) of the housing.

Section.name: Front nose / leading end cap
features included: Blend into side skins and bottom base
Section.function intent: Close the front end of the housing; provide a smooth leading profile and protect internal components.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a shell closure transferring membrane and bending loads into side skins and bottom base; curvature reduces stress concentrations.
Section.geometry: Single B-spline end-cap surface near the Z-min end of the part.
Section.location: Front/leading end of the housing (near Z-min).

major_faces.name: Front end-cap freeform
major_faces.description: B-spline closure surface forming the front/nose region (near Z-min), blending into bottom and sides.

Section.name: Rear tail / trailing end cap
features included: Blend into top deck and side skins
Section.function intent: Close the rear end of the housing; provide a smooth trailing profile and protect internal components.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as a shell closure; transfers bending/torsional loads from top deck and side skins across the trailing end.
Section.geometry: Single B-spline end-cap surface near the Z-max end of the part.
Section.location: Rear/trailing end of the housing (near Z-max).

major_faces.name: Rear end-cap freeform
major_faces.description: B-spline closure surface forming the rear/tail region (near Z-max), blending into the top deck and sides.

Section.name: Bottom base / underside
features included: Blend into side skins and end caps
Section.function intent: Provide the underside envelope and potential contact/stand surface; close the housing volume.
Section.physical behavior: Acts as the lower shell skin; carries compressive/contact loads and couples with side skins to resist bending and torsion.
Section.geometry: Large B-spline underside surface spanning most of the part length and width at low Y.

major_faces.name: Bottom freeform base
major_faces.description: Large B-spline underside surface at the lowest Y region; continuous along most of the length.

Section.name: Top aperture pocket (rectangular cutout/seat)
features included: Rectangular aperture/pocket defining the wheel/button seat
Section.function intent: Locate and constrain the wheel/button insert; provide clearance and define the external opening through which the wheel/button protrudes.
Section.physical behavior: Provides contact/locating planes that constrain the insert laterally; the pocket floor acts as a stop/support surface; surrounding walls react side loads from user actuation and transmit them into the shell.
Section.geometry: Set of planar faces forming a rectangular pocket: two opposing drafted side walls, two end walls, and a floor plane.
Section.location: Centered near the top deck region, roughly mid-length; opens through the top surface.

major_faces.name: Pocket left wall (drafted)
major_faces.description: Planar pocket wall on one lateral side of the aperture; slightly tilted (draft) relative to X.

major_faces.name: Pocket front wall
major_faces.description: Planar pocket end wall at one Z-side of the aperture.

major_faces.name: Pocket right wall (drafted)
major_faces.description: Planar pocket wall on the opposite lateral side of the aperture; slightly tilted (draft) relative to X.

major_faces.name: Pocket rear wall
major_faces.description: Planar pocket end wall at the opposite Z-side of the aperture.

major_faces.name: Pocket floor/stop plane
major_faces.description: Planar pocket floor (constant Y) providing a stop/support surface beneath the insert.

Section.name: Scroll-wheel / button insert
features included: Flat side faces defining wheel thickness
Rotation-capable interface (implied) with the pocket walls
Section.function intent: Provide a user-actuated control element (scroll wheel or rocker/button) accessible through the top aperture.
Section.physical behavior: Receives fingertip forces; rounded rim distributes contact pressure and improves ergonomics; rotates/rocks about an axis normal to its flat side faces (axis along X) while the pocket constrains translation.
Section.geometry: Compact insert comprised of two toroidal rim surfaces and two planar side faces (a rounded wheel-like solid).
Section.location: Seated in the top aperture near the upper central region; laterally centered and protruding above the top deck opening.

major_faces.name: Wheel left flat side
major_faces.description: Planar face (normal ~ -X) defining one flat side of the wheel/button.

major_faces.name: Wheel rim torus patch A
major_faces.description: Toroidal outer rim patch providing rounded edge/rolling contact surface (one side).

major_faces.name: Wheel right flat side
major_faces.description: Planar face (normal ~ +X) defining the opposite flat side of the wheel/button.

major_faces.name: Wheel rim torus patch B
major_faces.description: Second toroidal rim patch completing the rounded perimeter (opposite side).
